articles.title: Microsoft Outlook outage drags on for hours as attempts to restore service fail
articles.summary: A widespread outage involving Microsoft's Outlook email and other applications stretched into Friday morning as the company said it was working to restore service. The tech giant first posted a statement on social media saying it was "investigating reports of users experiencing issues" accessing online mailboxes shortly before 1 p.m. ET Thursday. Downdetector , which monitors outages, reported issues with Outlook, Teams and other products on Thursday, as Microsoft attempted to deploy several fixes. Los Angeles International Airport tower hit by power outage The company has been providing updates on steps to resolve the outage on its Microsoft 365 Status social media account , providing a window into the hourslong effort to troubleshoot the disruption. In a post shortly after 11:30 p.m. ET , the company said it was working on efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow. "We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery, so we're reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability," the post stated. Earlier in the day, the company said: "We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service." Adobe Stock - PHOTO: Microsoft 365 apps. Around 6 p.m. ET Thursday, the company said it was "returning a portion of affected servers to the service, and they remain stable so far," though later updated that the servers "can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic" and was working on a fix for that. California fire crews save Little League game from power outage Earlier, Microsoft also reported some users were experiencing issues with Microsoft Teams. The company shortly updated that "mitigative actions have successfully restored service health and functionality." Amid the outage, New York City's Emergency Management Department warned residents of potential delays in reaching city agencies. "If you are trying to contact a New York City agency by email or access an online City service that relies on Microsoft systems, you may experience delays or temporary disruptions," NYC Emergency Management said on social media. "These issues may affect the delivery of emails, responses from City agencies, and access to certain online services." For more urgent requests, the city advised residents to try using an alternative method to contact the agency, and to call 311 for non-emergency city services and 911 for emergencies. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/outlook-down-microsoft-outage-reported-mail/story?id=138088203

articles.title: SpaceX is trying to solve a decades-old challenge: Making rockets fully reusable
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 launches at Starbase in Texas on September 28, 2026 (RONALDO SCHEMIDT) Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit. A successful capture of the Starship upper stage would mark a significant milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable spacecraft that can drastically reduce mission costs and make frequent travel possible. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," SpaceX said. For the 15th Starship test flight Friday, SpaceX aims to recover both stages of the massive 124-meter (407-foot) launch vehicle. The company has caught the booster, dubbed Super Heavy, on three previous occasions, with the first stage descending vertically back to the launch site shortly after blastoff and nestling into mechanical "chopstick" arms. It will now attempt to do the same with the spaceship. Some versions of the vessel are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while others will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. A spacecraft that can be fully reused is the "Holy Grail" of the space industry, said Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "No one's really been able to do that so far," he said. "People have been trying to do that since the (NASA) space shuttle. But the space shuttle ended up being kind of a compromise because a lot of the vehicle wasn't reusable." Reusing the Starship spacecraft would require the vessel to withstand the extreme heat of reentering Earth's atmosphere and then return to service without extensive refurbishment. - Refueling challenge - Musk, the world's richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which are regularly employed to launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station. The Starship project, however, has been plagued by years-long delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges -- even as NASA is counting on the spaceship to serve as a lunar lander for its Artemis program. Other technical challenges include transferring fuel to Starship in orbit -- a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars. Following SpaceX's high-profile stock market debut in June, the company carried out the first orbital flight of Starship in September, though the mission was cut short due to an engine issue. It is also investing heavily in additional launch sites for its mega-rocket in Louisiana and Florida. - Complex capture - Friday's launch is scheduled to take place at SpaceX's "Starbase" in southern Texas at 4:45 pm (2245 GMT). Following liftoff and the mid-air separation of the two stages, SpaceX plans to bring Super Heavy back to Earth six and a half minutes later, catching it at the launch site on the Gulf of Mexico coastline. The spaceship will continue to reach Earth's orbit, where it will deploy 26 satellites into Musk's Starlink satellite internet constellation that has become a major revenue stream for SpaceX. It will then circle the planet 14 times, before returning 22 hours later and -- SpaceX hopes -- descending safely into the chopstick arms. This capture attempt is more complex than that of the booster, as the spaceship will be descending much faster and from a much greater altitude. SpaceX has said it would proceed with these maneuvers only if conditions are optimal, and in the past has made last-minute changes to test flights under Musk's "fail fast" strategy of learning through crashes, explosions and other mishaps. As of late Thursday, the US Federal Aviation Administration had not yet given its final approval for the test flight. cha-acb/mjf This article originally appeared on AFP at https://tech.yahoo.com/science/articles/spacex-starship-test-attempt-first-035915093.html

articles.title: 'How does a building just fall?' Neighbors grieve after Brooklyn building collapse.
articles.summary: What we know about the New York City building collapse Over the loud noise of her radio, Ann Marie did not hear the sound of the Brooklyn building behind her home collapse on Wednesday night, but she soon saw the flashing lights of fire department trucks rushing to the scene. When she made her way out to the wreckage, workers were still searching for bodies. One of the building's walls had torn off, exposing the inside of several apartment homes, and the rubble had collapsed into a construction site next door. At least eight of her neighbours died in the accident - six adults and two children, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. Five of the victims were residents, CBS reported. "Right now, I'm really scared," Marie told the BBC. "Now that I'm seeing exactly this side of the building, you can imagine the fright of those people, what happened to them." On Thursday afternoon, Mamdani said he had visited survivors in hospital. Eighteen people were injured, including four firefighters. One person is in critical condition. "I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost," Mamdani added. "These were our friends and our neighbours, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Trinidad and beyond." What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people Later on Thursday, a senior official with the New York Police Department identified the victims as Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9, Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31, Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10, Barry Mamadou, 23, and Ndiaye Mamadou, 31, according to CBS. They were residents of the building that collapsed. The other three victims lived elsewhere. Gabriel Siguencia, 22, lived in the Bronx, Edgar Sapon, 26, lived in Hell's Kitchen and Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26, lived in the Bushwick neighbourhood of Brooklyn. It was around 16:00 EST (21:00 GMT) on Wednesday when residents heard a loud boom as the 1930s building collapsed into a neighbouring construction site, where crews were working, according to fire department officials. Two construction workers were among the dead. The New York City Fire Department was on the scene within one minute of the emergency call, Mamdani said. Patricia Starek was waiting for her son to come home from school last night when she saw the helicopters near her home. The surge of the emergency responders initially brought back memories of New York during 2001 terrorist attacks. She has lived in Flatbush for 26 years, including during 9/11. "How does a building just fall into a pit? We all live here with the assumption that stairs are stable, floors are stable, that you can be on your third floor and not have the earth fall below you," she said. Mamdani said search conditions would grow more difficult with the rain in the morning, and responders continued their efforts for about 24 hours before determining on Thursday afternoon that there were no more victims at the site. Workers looked through the wreckage with drones, sniffer dogs, cranes and other equipment. Officials had said they would continue to search the wreckage until they were entirely certain there was no one left trapped, saying they still had big pieces of debris to remove. The mayor said city officials had identified the companies running the construction site, and were examining 100 other sites operated by the same groups to ensure they are safe. Contains some scenes which some viewers may find upsetting. - Video shows survivor being pulled from collapsed building in New York Dozens of residents gathered around the building on Thursday morning as debris floated through the air, and they watched in horror as workers tried to find more survivors or recover remains. The incident has rattled their calm and quiet neighbourhood, a melting pot of many New York immigrant communities including Afro-Caribbean, Hispanic and Asian residents. Joyette Kerr had been at the scene since midnight, praying with family members who were missing loved ones. Joyette Kerr was at the scene since midnight on Thursday consoling her neighbours [BBC] At 1:30 EST (6:30 GMT), Kerr watched emergency responders pull a survivor from the wreckage. At the church across the street, she consoled the wife of a young construction worker who died when the building fell on him. Rescuers recovered his body, Kerr said. "His wife was very hysterical," said Kerr, who has lived in the neighbourhood since she was a teenager. "She couldn't take the pain." She said another man had been frantically going to all the nearby hospitals to try to find his two nephews, but still had no answers. Footage showed another woman who was six-months pregnant being rescued from the rubble. "She is alive. She is still alive. I'm very happy. I'm very happy," her husband told the BBC's US partner CBS News. "I thank all of you guys." [BBC] Starek, the longtime Flatbush resident, said she was heading to the local YMCA where some family members were gathered to see if she could help - and many others in the neighbourhood were doing the same. "People look out for each other," Marie said. To lose eight of her neighbours, she said: "I can't believe it. There's a pain." Kerr said she hoped her hours with the victims' families brought them some measure of comfort after one of the deadliest building collapses in recent New York history. "It's going to be very profound," she said of the impact the accident will have. "Hopefully this will bring the community together." articles.title: Singapore's Megaspeed lawyers up with U.S. firm as Nvidia scandal broadens
articles.summary: SINGAPORE — A Singapore-based company at the center of the emerging scandal engulfing AI chipmaker Nvidia said Thursday that it has hired a U.S. law firm for what is likely to be a wave of intense legal and congressional scrutiny. Megaspeed, a cloud provider that employed a Chinese executive who had an affair with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said in a statement that the law firm would help to "independently verify its export control compliance practices." Megaspeed did not identify the law firm and did not immediately respond to requests for further comment. The company has been thrust into the global spotlight in recent weeks after revelations that the executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with the then-CEO of Nvidia and was suspected of being a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang resigned Thursday as members of Congress call for investigations into whether his relationship with the Megaspeed executive damaged U.S. national security. Megaspeed has been a major purchaser of advanced Nvidia chips that are covered by U.S. export controls. U.S. officials suspect the company smuggled Nvidia chips into China in violation of U.S. law, according to reports . The Megaspeed website, which is replete with references to Nvidia, lists three data centers vaguely located in "East South Asia." Southeast Asia is a major hub for chip smuggling . "Megaspeed has cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority," Megaspeed CEO James Tan Yong Pong said in a statement posted to the company's website. Tan said the "leading" U.S. law firm will also "lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units." GPUs are advanced chips used for artificial intelligence. POLITICO was unable to contact Megaspeed and its parent company, Swiftdata, earlier in the week after visiting the companies' offices . Swiftdata's listed office is occupied by an interior design firm. Tan has not responded to POLITICO requests via LinkedIn. Also on Thursday, the Singaporean government said it barred Huang from reentering the country earlier this year. "While Singapore does not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries, we expect all companies operating here to take into account such regulations, including export controls, in their international business activities," the Ministry of Home Affairs said. "Singapore does not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate other countries' export controls through fraud or dishonest practices." The statement said Huang was "investigated for suspected involvement in the possible offences in Singapore, given her position as then-CEO" of Megaspeed. A Singapore Police Force investigation into Megaspeed is ongoing. The Ministry of Home Affairs said it "has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company" from U.S. authorities. The Megaspeed episode is likely to boost Singaporean oversight and enforcement "to protect the country's reputation as a clean financial and logistics hub," Neil Shah, co-founder of tech-focused Counterpoint Research, told POLITICO. "We anticipate that Singapore's customs, corporate registries, and trade bodies will strengthen local checks and align with U.S. end-use reviews so the wider data center network avoids penalties tied to these shell intermediaries," he said. This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/megaspeed-lawyers-us-firm-nvidia-031513488.html

articles.title: Van Hollen takes on Schumer for majority leader after Democrats flip Senate
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections. Van Hollen said in a statement that “the American people called for change” and that is why he is running. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said. “This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.” Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win the race, which will be the first contested election for Senaet Democratic leader in decades. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December. The question of whether to reelect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators have declined to say publicly how they will vote, even before Van Hollen entered the race. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election and many are torn — Schumer recruited many of the party’s winning candidates and raised money for them, but progressive groups are pushing for his removal. Making the pitch for his reelection, Schumer has been working with Democratic senators one-on-one to form an agenda for 2027. In private caucus meetings this week, Schumer opened discussion on a broad plan for their first 100 days in power that included health care and tariff legislation and efforts to stop the Iran war. “I’m going to win it,” Schumer told The Associated Press in an interview last week. In a statement after Van Hollen’s announcement, Schumer said he welcomes any discussion about the future of the caucus. “I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.” Divisions over Schumer have simmered over the last two years While Schumer is the favorite to win, Van Hollen’s run exposes a rift in the party that opened in the spring of 2025 , when Schumer was put on the defensive after he sided with Republicans on a spending vote. Even as Schumer has redeemed himself within his caucus since then — leading them through a government shutdown last year and orchestrating huge wins in the election — many in the Democratic base are agitating for generational change. Van Hollen, 67, is not that much younger than Schumer, 75. But he has positioned himself as a new face in the party. He has also said he is considering a run for president. While most Democratic senators have either said they are supporting Schumer or are undecided, Van Hollen has at least two backers: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who won a competitive election in his state last week, and progressive standard bearer Bernie Sanders . El Sayed posted on X Thursday night that their majority will need “bold leadership.” “I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience,” El-Sayed wrote. “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.” Sen. Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, held a press conference Tuesday announcing he would not support Schumer. He posted Thursday night that the American people “want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats.” Van Hollen has not yet laid out his own agenda, but he has criticized Schumer for his ties to Israel and other special interests. While Schumer has a long history of support for Israel, he has strongly criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his handling of the war in Gaza. Schumer says he has broad support Several senators have said they are backing Schumer, including incoming Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown , who beat Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week. Beyond the election wins, those who support him say being the leader is a difficult job, experience is necessary and Schumer has proven himself with legislative successes when they held the Senate under President Joe Biden. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” posted Maine Sen. Angus King, another independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election. “Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible,” King wrote. Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto, D-Nev., also posted her support Thursday evening: Cortez Masto said Schumer was key in “securing a historic majority. I will be supporting him as our Democratic leader.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/sen-chris-van-hollen-maryland-020344480.html

articles.title: No charges for driver in Kansas soccer field incident that killed 2 people
articles.summary: The crash on Oct. 17 in Wichita killed a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man and injured 10 others. (Wyatt Glosson/KAKE / AP) A woman who killed two people, including a 6-year-old boy, when she drove through a Kansas soccer game last month had taken a nap in her parked vehicle before it accelerated and won’t be criminally charged, officials said Thursday. The Oct. 17 crash at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita killed the boy and a 35-year-old man, and injured 10 others when the vehicle drove through a soccer field at around 3:30 p.m. “I can not only find no evidence of an intentional crime, I can find affirmative evidence that there was not an intentional crime,” Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett said at a news conference. An off-duty police officer and others went to the truck after it had crashed and found the 34-year-old driver crying, Bennett said. Officials have not publicly identified the woman. “What they found was a sobbing — at turns described as frantic, hysterical — saying ‘I’m sorry, I’m sorry, what have I done,’ words to that effect,” Bennett said. He said the accounts of the people who were there that day said “she was sleepy, looked like she had just woken up, these are comments from witnesses who arrived there at the door and interacted with her.” The woman got up around 6 a.m. and drove her husband’s truck from Garden City, around 200 miles away, to the sports complex where her children had games, officials said. She was not in her usual vehicle because hers had issues with tire air pressure, Sullivan said. Bennett and Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan called it a tragedy that has shaken the community. Sullivan said the investigation was thorough and fact-driven, and that “every lead was examined, every piece of evidence was reviewed.” “I also want to be honest with our community: There are some questions we may never be able to answer with complete certainty,” he said. Among them was whether the pickup was in park. The driver told her kids she was going to take a nap, and reclined the seat, Sullivan said. One child went to warm up for a game and the second, a 14-year-old, put a sunshade over the windshield so people couldn’t look in on the sleeping mother, officials said. The vehicle later accelerated and drove straight onto the soccer field. The truck was parked in a stall, with a 7-inch curb in front, with a straight line toward a sideline area, Bennett said. Investigators explored whether the woman may have been asleep and moved in her sleep and put the vehicle from park into drive. Bennett said that’s possible but unlikely because the foot would need to be on the brake to change gears and there would be other steps, and the gear shift is loud. The other scenario is that the truck was not placed in park and she did not realize it, and later accelerated, he said. Police did a recreation with a similar make and model, and an officer of similar proportions of the driver, and in that test the truck — while in drive — rested at the curb but did not go over, Bennett said. “Her child does say at one point she kind of turns, goes from her back to her side,” he said. “And if her foot comes forward and hits that accelerator, that’s all that has to take place for that to be the explanation.” The woman told police that she believes she put the vehicle in park, Bennett said. One of the children said their mother went to sleep, and “next thing they know, the truck is leaping forward,” he said. “Mom says she wakes to, her kids are screaming, she looks up, she’s disoriented, she’s trying to sit up from a completely relaxed position to sit forward,” Bennett said. “Reaches for the steering wheel, looks up, sees shades that were not there when she went to sleep, batting at them.” The driver was cooperative and voluntarily gave blood after the crash, which tested negative for any intoxicating substances, Sullivan said. Police also examined her medical records, reviewed her social media, and had a General Motors engineer and technician examine the vehicle for any mechanical failures after the crash, Sullivan said. No mechanical problems were found, and the vehicle was not under any recalls, he said. The woman and her children had been at the complex most of the day, arriving in the morning, police said. Refs, coaches, and other people there were interviewed and no one reported any conflicts, Bennett said. “No one had a problem with this woman,” he said. Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, both of McPherson, Kansas, were killed. They were not related. The families of the victims and those injured were contacted by police and the district attorney’s office to inform them of the findings before the news conference, officials said. “There are families, friends, witnesses, first responders and members of this community who will forever carry the weight of that day,” Sullivan said. articles.title: D.C. shooting suspect was suing his condo association. Man killed was the building manager.
articles.summary: WASHINGTON – As police investigate why a board-certified emergency physician might have opened fire in a Washington, DC, neighborhood Nov. 12, they pointed to a lawsuit against his homeowners association as potentially playing a role. Police said Matt Wade Lambert, a 55-year-old healthcare professional, shot and killed his building manager, James Stuart, in a DC gym before barricading himself inside his apartment and shooting four additional people from his patio early in the morning on Nov. 12. Lambert also shot and killed himself, police said. One of the shooting victims remains in critical condition, while the other three do not have life threatening injuries, police said. Those who knew Lambert said they were shocked. His professional acquaintances described Lambert as a “genuine” and “good” person in conversations with USA TODAY. His attorney, Joel Braithwaite, said during a news conference that life appeared to be looking up for Lambert before the shooting, noting that he was scheduled to begin a new job Nov. 16. Braithwaite said Lambert gave no indication that he was at a breaking point during a phone conversation they had Nov. 10. Lambert, who worked as a consultant for healthcare administrators, had spoken at a conference in Orlando, earlier in the week. Craig Hauben, a fellow panelist at the event and the CEO of the software development firm Clutch, said Lambert seemed “jovial” at the time. He did not mention anything about ongoing litigation with his building, Hauben said. Court documents reveal Lambert has been enmeshed in litigation with his condo association since 2025 over water damage and black mold in his unit that he said stemmed from construction to the building. Lambert’s dispute with Metropole Condominium Association Back in March 2023, the HOA began work on the condo's façade to remediate the building envelope, according to a court filing by Lambert against the Metropole Condominium Association on March 21, 2025. Between May 2023 and April 2024, Lambert paid the association’s special assessment for the building envelope remediation that totaled $15,356.95, according to court documents. During the construction, Lambert said his “unit experienced suspected water intrusion, mold, significant moisture accumulation, and/or related damage,” according to the March 21, 2025 court filing. Lambert said he communicated to the association that there were instances of water intrusion in his unit in March 2024. A hole was cut into the drywall in Lambert’s residence in August 2024 to investigate whether water was running behind the wall, according to court filings. By September 2024, Lambert alleged in court documents that there was excess moisture being collected behind the drywall and his electrical curtains had stopped working. He also said that same month that mold was visible and detectable by smell, according to the court filings. He retained mold remediation expert ServPro on Sept. 20, 2024 to conduct an assessment of suspected mold that was visible from the hole that building officials cut above his windows back in August 2024. The inspection said: “Visible mold contamination was observed on exterior and interior walls, due to possible water intrusion,” according to an excerpt included in the filings. Lambert on Oct. 9, 2024 asked the Metropole Condominium Association to take action against the mold and excess moisture based on the independent inspections, as well as provide reimbursement for the costs of the assessments. Lambert said in court documents that he incurred expenses in excess of $82,000 "as a result of Defendant’s inaction to remedy any of the effect of its building envelope repair on Unit 704." Later in October 2024, Lambert and the condo association traded letters over the repairs that Lambert was going to do and whether he would be refunded by the group. The back-and-forth between Lambert and the condo association spiraled into a more than yearlong legal battle that included Stuart, the building manager, as a witness, as well as VIDA Fitness as a defendant. According to court documents, VIDA, located on the ground floor of the condo building, would use commercial dryers that Lambert alleged would “discharge warm, moist air that is vented up through a mechanical shaft to a dryer vent fan on the roof.” An engineering consulting firm hired by another plaintiff found that the elevated moisture levels in Lambert’s apartment were likely caused by the dryers, according to the court filing. USA TODAY could not immediately reach the attorneys for the condo association or VIDA Fitness. Braithwaite said he does not know what might have triggered Lambert ahead of the shooting. He noted it was the anniversary of when Lambert buried his mother. “I don't think there's any sense to be made,” Braithwaite said. “There's nothing that I can say from my mind that brings any closure to it.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: What court documents reveal about DC shooting suspect's HOA issues This article originally appeared on USA TODAY at https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/crime/2026/11/12/dc-shooting-what-we-know/92746956007/

articles.title: Jensen Huang's resignation and its impact on Nvidia and the AI industry
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his top post at the chipmaker he co-founded, after reports of the tech titan's extramarital affairs came into the spotlight this week. One of those relationships has raised national security concerns . The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with a businesswoman U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, which Beijing denies . Separately, the outlet and later others reported that Nvidia employees said Huang had another affair with an executive who reported to him directly — compounding calls for him to step down. Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Thursday, effective immediately. The California-based company said that Colette Kress — who has been Nvidia's chief financial officer and executive vice president since 2013 — will step into the role of interim CEO. The scandal marks the most tumultuous chapter yet for Nvidia, whose high-end chips have emerged as the leading building blocks for artificial intelligence. Huang himself has become a key face in the AI race, both across the industry and often on U.S. President Donald Trump’s side in Washington. Here's what we know. Nvidia's new leadership Nvidia said Kress is now interim CEO . Prior to joining Nvidia over 13 years ago, Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. In a statement about her new post on Thursday, Kress said Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she's “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” Huang co-founded Nvidia, alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, back in 1993 — and until Thursday had led the company ever since, with no clear successor in sight. Huang's ouster has led to a scramble for a new permanent CEO, and Nvidia said it's considering both “internal and external candidates.” The company's board of directors also said Thursday that it has named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Jones. Affairs in the spotlight Over the weekend, following news reports of Huang's relationship with a woman identified as former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang , Nvidia's then-CEO apologized for being “unfaithful to my wife.” "My actions hurt her and our children,” Huang wrote in a Sunday email to employees, adding that his colleagues also “deserve better” from him. Neither Huang nor Nvidia identified who he had been intimate with by name, but the apology arrived shortly after Nvidia said it was investigating whether Huang had been “the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. (Huang is a common surname and the two are not related). Nvidia initially maintained Huang would stay on as CEO as the company conducted its investigation. But scrutiny grew late Wednesday after reports emerged that Huang had a separate affair with an Nvidia executive. Huang’s resignation arrived shortly after. The company didn't address either relationship in its Thursday announcement. Later on Thursday, Reuters reported Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, citing unidentified sources. Where investigations stand Nvidia hasn't provided any notable new updates in its internal review announced Sunday. At the time, the company said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Trump was reportedly briefed about intelligence findings involving Huang well before the scandal erupted publicly. But when asked over the weekend whether he wished he had acted sooner on that information, the president said “I don’t think so” and maintained that Nvidia’s CEO was an “honorable guy.” Trump later said the FBI is looking into Huang's affair with Alice Huang, although where exactly that probe stands is unclear. Meanwhile, lawmakers from both sides of the aisle on Capitol Hill are calling for further investigations. Many eyes have been on Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously" — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government. Singaporean authorities said they questioned Alice Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed. They concluded there wasn’t enough evidence that she had committed a crime, but suspected she provided “inaccurate information” to downplay her role at Megaspeed. Malaysia said Friday it was investigating whether any of the chips brought into Malaysia by Megaspeed or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix had been reexported to other country. China, meanwhile, has denied that it attempted to ensnare Jensen Huang. Its Foreign Ministry earlier this week called the spying allegations “unsubstantiated” and said they amount to a smear campaign against Beijing. Trump continues his praise for Huang Huang has maintained a close relationship to Trump throughout the Republican president’s second term in office. He’s successfully lobbied for looser AI regulation overall — including less strict limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. And he's among tech CEOs who have dined at the White House, and even traveled on Air Force One . Trump has called Huang “smart” and “amazing,” repeatedly insisting he join him on foreign trips. After news of his resignation broke on Thursday, the president maintained that Huang had “done a fantastic job.” He also chimed in with his own recommendation for Nvidia's CEO seat: former chief executive of Apple Tim Cook , who has similarly remained in Trump's orbit over recent years. “There is only one man to take his place,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform Thursday. “Legend replaces a Legend!” Critics quickly decried Trump's comments. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the Republican administration had “repeatedly undermined the free market economy” and that Thursday marked the latest example of “Donald Trump weighing in on behalf of his views connected to corporate America, as opposed to focusing on working class America.” A new test for the AI industry The shockwaves of Huang's exit stress just how few figures hold so much power the AI race. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable companies today — and Huang himself (often wearing his signature leather jacket) has risen to fame across the tech world. Some analysts suspect the foreign intelligence allegations will strengthen calls in Washington for stricter export controls with China, which could in turn renew trade strains overall. Others have called it a watershed moment for Nvidia, the chipmaker that has long been seen as the crown jewel for powering AI. And questions of security risks facing the companies at the forefront of this technology are piling up. Nvidia shares fell more than 4% by market close Thursday, after plummeting earlier in the day. Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for Forrester, said Huang’s resignation from Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole. “If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience," she said. “If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.” ______ AP Writers Kelvin Chan, Chan Ho-him, Mae Anderson and Lisa Mascaro contributed. articles.title: Trump says 'we don't need a deal with Iran' and that Vance should focus on Democrats
articles.summary: By Bo Erickson WASHINGTON, Nov 12 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete ‌and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. Trump's directive came a day after the Wall ‌Street Journal reported that Vance was considering face-to-face peace talks with a hard-line Iranian security official and a week after the vice president blamed the costly war with ​Iran for Republicans' midterm elections drubbing. "We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!" Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Strait of Hormuz. Trump had suggested in recent weeks that Iran would be more willing to strike a deal in the eight-month conflict after the US elections, but his administration this week ‌signaled it believes its blockade and economic sanctions ⁠against Iran are working, meaning neither a military escalation nor diplomacy is needed. The US military is imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, while attempting to secure safe passage for international shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz. ⁠Iran's military said on Thursday four oil tankers were hit by explosions after they ignored Iranian warnings. Vance's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. VANCE HAD LED IRAN DIPLOMACY Vance, long seen as skeptical of the war the US and Israel launched on Iran in February, led talks with Iranian officials ​in ​Pakistan in April that produced a June memorandum of understanding that paused ​the war but broke down within weeks. Iranian state media said ‌late last month Tehran had received a letter from Vance seeking renewed talks with Washington. Trump said he had not directed his vice president to make the outreach. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday after talks with US allies in Paris that Iran's demands for a potential deal were "absurd," citing its demand for reparations for the war, and said Trump would not sign a bad deal. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance was considering meeting with a senior Iranian security official, a move that would have put Vance at the ‌center of peace negotiations. Reuters has not confirmed the potential talks. Vance, who is ​viewed as a leading contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, distanced himself ​from the war last week after Republicans' midterm election rout ​by Democrats. The vice president blamed the costs of the Iran war in part for the party's losses. He ‌also said an earlier recommendation to end the war ​was "sound advice." Trump responded to Vance's position ​by defending the war as necessary to stop Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. In his social media post, Trump said he had asked Vance to focus instead on a domestic issue the president previously put in his portfolio: leading an effort targeting alleged ​fraud in Democratic-run cities and states throughout the ‌US. "Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large-scale criminal activity. CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s ​blood!" Trump wrote on Thursday. (Reporting by Bo Erickson in Washington; additional reporting by Simon Lewis, Doina Chiacu and Susan ​HeaveyEditing by Colleen Jenkins, Andrea Ricci, Don Durfee and Nia Williams) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-says-vance-focus-domestic-133908907.html

articles.title: Hegseth honors guard who scolded his group at the Tomb of Unknown Soldier
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday honored the Army sentinel who forcefully scolded members of his entourage for laughing and talking near Arlington National Cemetery's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day. Hegseth posted a photo of himself on social media pinning a Joint Service Commendation Medal on the unidentified soldier's chest. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," Hegseth wrote. "Carry on Patriots." On Veterans Day, Hegseth, his wife Jennifer, and three of his top deputies were seen posing for photographs on the steps overlooking the tomb, which has provided a final resting place for several of America's unidentified service members — and a site of reflection and mourning — since 1921. Members of the group could be heard chuckling and chatting as they ascended the steps. We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots. pic.twitter.com/Uk6ek6oOso — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth (@SecWar) November 12, 2026 The sentinel — a member of the Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as The Old Guard — stepped forward and shouted in their direction: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!" Video of the encounter, which followed the annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, spread quickly online. A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery. As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be… pic.twitter.com/dIPp8wMGEG — The Associated Press (@AP) November 11, 2026 On Wednesday evening, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell issued a statement saying the soldier had acted appropriately. "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell said. Joint Service Commendation Medals are awarded to members of the Armed Forces who distinguish themselves while serving in a joint activity or on joint military staff. Hegseth's Veterans Day flap follows his brush with impeachment earlier this week . On Tuesday, the Republican-controlled U.S. House of Representatives voted to effectively kill the articles of impeachment against Hegseth — for now — by blocking their consideration on the House floor and sending them back to the Judiciary Committee, where GOP leaders can hold them up until the next Congress is seated in January 2027. Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, reintroduced impeachment charges against Hegseth on Monday, alleging that the embattled Pentagon chief had committed "high crimes and misdemeanors" and abused the power of his office by violating the War Powers Resolution, conducting military operations without congressional authorization and ordering unlawful military actions in several countries. Democrats — who voted unanimously against shelving the impeachment charges — will have a large House majority next year after winning at least 255 seats in last week's midterm elections. They have already vowed to try to remove Hegseth from office when they take control of Congress, building on voter dissatisfaction with the war in Iran. "In the majority, one of the first things we're gonna do is run Pete Hegseth out of town," Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader who is poised to become House speaker, said at a rally last month . Hegseth would be just the third Cabinet official in U.S. history to be impeached , and the second in three years. articles.summary: 美国财政状况在10月明显恶化。作为2027财年的首月，10月美国财政赤字创下历史同期最高纪录，财政开局创下历年最差表现。 美国财政部最新数据显示， 10月美国财政赤字达到4040亿美元，较去年同期的2840亿美元大幅扩大，也远超9月的270亿美元。赤字激增主要受到国防支出异常增长和债务利息支出持续攀升的双重推动。 与此同时，政府收入同比下降8.8%，进一步扩大了财政收支缺口。 更值得关注的是，美国债务利息负担已达到新的危险水平。 过去12个月，联邦政府利息支出占税收收入的比例升至28.2%，创历史新高，意味着政府每征收1美元税款，就有超过28美分用于支付债务利息。 收入增长乏力，支出扩张加速，财政缺口持续扩大 10月，美国政府总收入为3690亿美元，较上年同期的4040亿美元下降8.8%。其中，个人所得税收入为1860亿美元，约占总收入的一半；社会保险及退休金收入为1310亿美元，是另一主要收入来源。 从更长周期来看，政府收入增长正在明显放缓。 过去12个月滚动口径下，收入增速仅为1.1%，远低于疫情后相当长一段时间内的两位数增长水平。历史数据显示，每当这一滚动增速转为负值，美国经济往往已经陷入衰退或接近衰退。 支出端则呈现相反趋势。10月政府总支出达到7730亿美元，较上年同期的6887亿美元增长约12%。按照过去6个月滚动口径计算，政府支出规模已升至6490亿美元，为疫情冲击期间以外的历史最高水平，距离疫情期间的绝对纪录也仅差约500亿美元。 收入增长放缓与支出持续扩张形成鲜明反差。 过去五年，美国政府支出不断攀升，而收入增长相对停滞，财政收支之间的缺口持续扩大。 国防支出异常激增，债务利息负担再创新高 国防支出的异常增长是10月赤字扩大的重要推手之一。 当月国防支出大幅攀升，增长幅度明显偏离常规季节性走势，成为财政赤字超预期扩张的重要原因。 不过，财政部目前尚未披露此次支出激增的具体构成，其背后原因仍有待进一步厘清。 与此同时，债务利息支出继续攀升。 10月联邦政府单月利息支出达到1155亿美元，创历年10月最高纪录。 按照过去12个月滚动口径计算，美国联邦政府利息支出已达到1.4万亿美元，占税收收入的28.2%，两项指标均处于历史高位。按照当前趋势，2027财年全年利息支出可能达到1.6万亿美元甚至更高。 这意味着债务利息正在挤占越来越多的财政资源。 预计到2027年底，利息支出规模将与社会保障支出大体相当，成为联邦政府最大的单项支出之一。 考虑到社会保障体系本身也面临长期偿付压力，两项刚性支出的同步增长将进一步压缩政府的财政腾挪空间。 此外， 12月通常是美国全年债务利息支出最高的月份，季节性因素意味着未来几个月财政负担仍可能进一步加重。 2027财年开局创纪录，长期财政可持续性承压 综合来看，2027财年首月，美国财政赤字、10月债务利息支出以及财年开局赤字规模均创下历史同期纪录，反映出美国财政收支失衡正在进一步加深。 一方面，税收收入增长明显放缓，政府收入缺乏足够动力；另一方面，国防等支出增加，加上不断膨胀的债务利息，使财政支出持续承压。 尤其是利息支出占税收收入的比例不断攀升，意味着美国政府越来越多的财政收入被用于偿债，而非公共服务和其他政策领域。 在债务规模与融资成本双双高企的背景下，美国财政可持续性面临更大考验。财政赤字持续扩大也可能加剧市场对美国长期债务供给、国债收益率及未来货币政策走向的关注。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “这是世代级错误”“没人能替代他”“不会再买英伟达股票”！黄仁勋走了，硅谷吵翻了 ，Twitter前CEO预测他3年后王者归来
articles.summary: 北京时间2026年11月12日，这一晚注定会被写进科技史。 33年前，一个亚洲面孔在硅谷的车库里创办了一家芯片公司。33年后，他亲手将这家公司送上了全球市值之巅。然后，在一个普通的周四早晨，被自己的董事会扫地出门—— 英伟达创始人黄仁勋，正式辞去CEO职务。 消息传出的那一刻，科技圈、华尔街、华盛顿，几乎所有人都停下手头的事，开始争论同一个问题： 这到底是英伟达的自救，还是一场无法挽回的历史性错误？ 有人说，这是一个时代的终结 黄仁勋传记作者斯蒂芬·维特（Stephen Witt）在CNBC上说出了很多人心里的话： "黄仁勋就是英伟达。就像公牛队没有乔丹。我不知道他们怎么替代这个人。" 他还讲了一个细节： 黄仁勋能凭记忆徒手画出英伟达设备的每一个零件爆炸图——"这种人，我不知道他们怎么替代。" Shopify创始人兼CEO托比·吕特克（Tobi Lütke）称，这次CEO更迭是"世代级错误"（generational blunder）。他警告说，英伟达可能会沦为他所创造的那家公司的一个拙劣模仿： " 没有人能替代像黄仁勋这样的创始人。 " 著名投资人纳瓦尔·拉维坎特（Naval Ravikant）引用了两个历史案例——苹果开除乔布斯、Uber逼走卡兰尼克——反问道：" 我们难道还没学到，你不可能简单地替换掉一个创始人吗？ "马斯克在下面回复了两个词： "True words."（所言甚是。） 有人说，英伟达还会好 科技界大牛、CNBC主持人吉姆·克莱默（Jim Cramer）一向以嗓门大、反应快著称。这次他没有绕弯子："不得不这样做。证据太多了。" 他随即称赞被董事会任命为临时CEO的科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）： " 我很欣赏科莱特，我认为她会出色地把局面稳住。 " 资产管理公司Gerber Kawasaki的CEO罗斯·格伯（Ross Gerber）自称是"长期英伟达投资者"，他把这一刻类比为乔布斯离开时：" 那时很多人以为苹果完了。结果不过是个开始。 "他说，AI会继续，英伟达会继续，只是这个时刻确实令人痛心。 加密投资人安东尼·庞普利亚诺（Anthony Pompliano）则更激进："今天很可能就是AI抛售潮的底部。全球最大公司CEO辞职——这已经是最大程度的投降信号了。" 有人说，他们会永远站在黄仁勋这边 然而，更多的声音，是惋惜。 Perplexity AI创始人阿拉文德·斯里尼瓦斯（Aravind Srinivas）发帖致谢： "感谢黄仁勋33年的勇敢领导。你把一家小初创公司建成了美国最有价值的公司……你对我这样的创始人所给予的时间和建议，为AI的未来奠定了基础。" 马斯克转发了《AIR》电影台词——"你将永远被铭记，因为有些东西是永恒的"——并附上了一个名字： "Jensen。" 前高盛CEO劳尔德·贝兰克梵（Lloyd Blankfein）则引用了一句据称出自戴高乐的名言： "为黄仁勋感到惋惜。莎士比亚式的悲剧。但正如戴高乐所说——'墓地里躺满了不可或缺的人。'" 币安创始人赵长鹏直接写道： "英伟达让黄仁勋离开，是个错误。" Lex Fridman的帖子是当天最长、情绪最浓烈的一篇。他说，英伟达放走黄仁勋"是苹果开除乔布斯故事的重演，但影响更大"，因为AI对人类未来的意义无可比拟。他说自己和黄仁勋相处多年，见过他在镜头之外、面对普通人时展现出的谦逊与善意：" 我从未听任何认识他的人说过半句坏话，这包括数百名工程师、CEO、朋友……大概超过一千人。 "他说：我站在黄仁勋这边。 Epic Games的创始人蒂姆·斯维尼（Tim Sweeney）写道：" 这是英伟达、开发者、美国和全人类的悲哀之日。 "——马斯克也转发了这条帖子。 有人继续看多，有人拒绝再买 市场永远是实用主义的。 新加坡亿万富翁Leo KoGuan持有约13亿美元的英伟达股份。消息出来后，他在X上发帖，直接、明确，没有任何修辞：" 没有黄仁勋，我不会再增持了。 " 他把黄仁勋称为"至高无上的创造者"，并写道："美国是创造者的文明。我们珍视、颂扬并奖励创造者。创造者第一，监管者第二，分销者第三。今天，我们把监管者放在了第一位。" 他说，如果黄仁勋将来创立或收购了一家新公司，他希望有机会参与投资。 分析师丹·艾夫斯（Dan Ives）同样认为董事会没有选择余地。就在辞职消息正式宣布之前，他已经给出了自己的估值判断： " 没有黄仁勋，英伟达股票价值225美元；有他，就是300美元。 " 分析师吉恩·芒斯特（Gene Munster）的帖子简洁直白："未知的现在已经明朗了。今早英伟达股价会跳空低开，底部在150美元附近，然后市场会把注意力转回真正重要的事情上来。" 他补充说，AI需求仍在加速，英伟达GPU依然是明确的赢家。 国内知名投资人段永平也表态 ，不会卖出英伟达，并在消息公布当日卖出大量认沽期权（Puts）。他认为，英伟达可能邀请黄仁勋担任顾问，成为类似“影子CEO”的角色，保留影响力，只是不再拥有签字决策权，而这个方向，要等到听证会结束之后才有可能出现明确结论。 三年后，他会回来吗？ 也许最有趣的预测来自Twitter的前CEO迪克·科斯特洛（Dick Costolo）。他发帖写道： "我的预测：3到4年后，英伟达会有一两个季度的业绩不及预期，然后他们会把黄仁勋请回来重新掌舵。就像名人的丑闻一样，所有人愤慨15分钟，然后就过去了。而美国人最喜欢的，就是王者归来的故事。等着看。" 这段话在网上迅速传播。有人嘲笑它天真，有人说它看穿了一切。 毕竟，乔布斯1985年被逐出苹果，1997年又回来了，然后带来了iPhone。 Hugging Face的CEO克莱门特·德朗格（Clem Delangue）的话，或许是整件事里最简单也最真实的总结。他的公司正在被英伟达以129亿美元收购，这笔交易的未来现在也多了一个问号。他在社交媒体上写道："整件事太糟糕了。我希望这一切都没发生。这真的是令人悲伤的一天。" 然后，他话锋一转，宣布会继续推动开源AI事业——"比以往任何时候都更努力"。 这大概也是黄仁勋留下来的东西的一部分： 那些他点燃的人，还在继续燃烧。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 中东原油“全面夺回”亚洲市场，美国至亚洲油轮运价从高点跌61%
articles.summary: 中东原油流向亚洲正在回升，亚洲炼油商的采购重心逐步转回传统供应来源，美国原油的替代性需求随之减弱。 11月13日，据彭博报道， 美国墨西哥湾至亚洲航线的超大型原油运输船（VLCC）日收益较10月峰值下跌61%，而波斯湾至东亚航线的同类指标仅下跌24%，两条航线运价走势明显分化。 采购数据也印证了这一趋势。日本、泰国等亚洲炼油商正在重启或扩大中东原油采购。彭博此前报道称，亚洲炼油商订购的11月交付美国原油数量较此前骤降约50%，至2400万至2600万桶。 据报道援引知情交易员， 来自阿联酋、沙特阿拉伯和卡塔尔的原油流量均已显著扩大，其中包括需要穿越霍尔木兹海峡运输的货物。 随着中东产油国产量恢复、售价下调，亚洲原油进口格局正逐步回归美伊冲突前的状态。 中东供应恢复，产油国下调售价争夺市场 今年2月美伊冲突爆发初期，途经霍尔木兹海峡的油轮遭到袭击，波斯湾产油国原油出口大幅收缩，亚洲买家被迫转向美国等替代供应来源。 随着局势趋于稳定，中东原油供应逐步恢复。 沙特阿拉伯向欧佩克报告称，其10月原油产量升至近年来的月度高位之一。 与此同时，主要产油国也在通过降价争夺亚洲市场份额。沙特近期将面向亚洲买家的官方售价下调至六年来低位；已于4月退出欧佩克的阿联酋，也下调了12月交付旗舰原油品种的价格溢价。 荷兰国际集团（ING Groep NV）大宗商品策略主管Warren Patterson表示， 亚洲很难摆脱对中东这一最大原油供应来源的依赖，因为全球供需平衡中缺乏足够的额外供应，难以支持采购来源的大规模转移。 亚洲买家回流中东，美国原油订单减少 日本炼油商已经开始增加中东原油采购。Eneos Holdings和Cosmo Energy Holdings近期均有采购阿联酋原油的记录。 乐天证券经济研究所分析师Yutaro Nishi表示，只要日本炼油商仍能从中东获得原油，就很可能继续采购。 他指出，尽管各国情况有所不同，但亚洲仍将是中东原油的主要市场。 印度的采购结构也出现变化。根据Kpler数据，来自波斯湾的原油进口量已超过俄罗斯，重新成为印度最大的原油进口来源。 与中东采购回升相对应，美国原油对亚洲的出口需求明显降温。 科珀斯克里斯蒂港首席执行官Kent Britton本周表示，上周从美国墨西哥湾沿岸出发的40艘原油油轮中，没有一艘驶往亚洲。 美国至亚洲航线VLCC日收益较10月峰值下跌61%，而波斯湾至东亚航线仅下跌24%，也反映出两条航线运输需求的不同变化。亚洲炼油商重新增加中东采购，正在推动原油贸易流向向冲突前的格局回归。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 微软服务全球大宕机：Outlook报障超13万条，紧急抢修正在进行中
articles.summary: 微软正紧急抢修旗下多项核心服务，此次全球性宕机事件波及企业、政府机构及普通用户，是该公司近几个月来最严重的技术故障之一。 据英国《金融时报》11月13日报道， 故障自周四开始蔓延，持续至周五，导致Outlook电子邮件服务、Teams协作平台、Copilot AI助手及其他Microsoft 365服务大面积中断。 故障监测平台Downdetector显示，Outlook问题报告在峰值时段突破 13万条 。微软周五在X平台表示，正致力于将服务恢复至“健康状态”，并已出现“部分恢复”迹象。 此次宕机对全球多个行业造成直接冲击。瑞士奢侈品集团历峰宣布，因此次故障推迟发布半年度业绩；美国电动卡车制造商Workhorse Group亦于周四推迟发布季度财报。部分企业表示，通讯中断已影响到日常业务运转。与此同时，美国、澳大利亚、日本及新加坡等多国政府机构均受到波及。 微软：无迹象显示遭受恶意攻击 微软Copilot、Agents与平台业务执行副总裁Charles Lamanna在X平台发文表示，目前 没有迹象显示此次故障源于“恶意行为或网络攻击” 。 此次宕机对多国政府运作造成干扰。 澳大利亚警方及情报机构 均受到影响；日本内阁官房副长官Masanao Ozaki发出警告，称依赖微软系统的日本政府共享IT基础设施正遭遇中断。 新加坡当局表示，部分政府系统受到影响，但强调 紧急服务维持全面正常运转 。印度工人在延长的排灯节假期结束返岗后，也在社交媒体上纷纷反映遭遇微软服务中断问题。 日本：银行证券机构重启传真机 日本是此次宕机中受影响最为显著的市场之一。随着日本员工陆续开始工作日，Downdetector记录到逾 4600条 Microsoft 365相关问题报告及逾 3500条 Outlook问题报告，此后随着时间推移数字有所回落。 多家日本企业向英国《金融时报》表示，Outlook故障导致电子邮件出现延迟。物流集团佐川急便（Sagawa Express）被迫暂停全国各地火车站及机场行李寄存服务的当日预约。据日本当地媒体报道，部分银行及证券机构不得不 重新启用传真机 来确认交易。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄仁勋的下台是硅谷权利流失的标志
articles.summary: 英伟达联合创始人黄仁勋的被迫下台，打破了大型科技公司不可战胜的神话，标志着硅谷权力结构正在发生深刻的转移。 科技巨头不再庞大且不受约束，传统的官僚机构、制度权力以及旧有规范正在重新确立统治地位。 据华尔街日报11月12日报道，这位将英伟达精准布局于AI核心地位、并使其跻身全球最具价值公司之列的创始人，在丑闻发酵后短短数日内便宣告离任。 这一突发事件直接导致英伟达股价持续下挫，并引发了投资者对市场可能面临痛苦回调的深切担忧。 对于许多将英伟达算力视为行业风向标的投资者而言，核心人物的离去为整个AI领域带来了巨大的不确定性。 面对这一震动，科技界高管纷纷表达支持，试图捍卫这位在AI军备竞赛中掌握生杀大权的关键人物。 然而，这种抱团防御的姿态不仅凸显了科技行业对不计代价追求胜利的执念，也暴露出其本能反应与当前政治和制度现实的脱节。 随着华盛顿权力格局的更迭，科技巨头在政治上的影响力正在流失。 在民主党于中期选举中获胜后，美国立法者明确表示，从明年1月起将对科技行业施加更严厉的审查，国家安全已成为压倒一切的监管焦点。 创始人神话的终结与市场震荡 黄仁勋巧妙地将英伟达定位在AI繁荣的核心，使其成为全球市值最高的公司之一。 他的迅速离职不仅是对硅谷长期秉持的“现代创始人至关重要”信念的沉重打击，更引发了资本市场的直接动荡。 报道称，对特定科技领袖而言，失去黄仁勋意味着失去了一个能决定其AI雄心成败的重要个人关系。英伟达芯片在AI领域引发了惊人的支出和投资，但也促成了一些存在隐患的交易，市场担忧这可能引发剧烈的调整期。 创业加速器Y Combinator负责人 Garry Tan 在X平台上发文指出，考虑到黄仁勋的领导力对未来运营的核心作用，英伟达董事会罢免他的决定似乎是不明智的。 AngelList联合创始人 Naval Ravikant 将其与史蒂夫·乔布斯和从Uber黯然下台的Travis Kalanick相提并论，感叹“不能简单地替换创始人”，这一观点得到了马斯克的赞同。 Travis Kalanick本人更是发布了应对“现代政变或批斗会”的建议。 硅谷精英的本能防御与文化冲突 面对更具破坏性的指控，许多科技精英在黄仁勋正式宣布辞职前就开始为其辩护，呼吁由股东投票决定其未来或等待调查结束。部分科技界人士将黄仁勋的困境视为政府、竞争对手或外国势力推动的“心理战”。 Anduril Industries联合创始人Palmer Luckey和红杉资本合伙人Shaun Maguire均强调这是关于美国在AI领域获胜的问题。 然而，这种本能的防御遭到了行业内部的严厉反思。曾为马斯克和马克·扎克伯格工作的非营利组织Center for Tomorrow创始人Dex Hunter-Torricke表示： “即使面临更多指控，这些科技领袖的第一直觉仍是抱团防御，这表明了科技界内部痴迷于胜利的文化腐败，这种本能在新的政治现实中将不再奏效。” 政治审查加剧与地缘博弈 科技亿万富翁的权力在中期选举中受到了严峻考验，AI数据中心成为主要的竞选议题。过去两年中，以马斯克、黄仁勋为代表的广泛AI领导层在特朗普政府时期蓬勃发展。然而，随着民主党乘着“蓝色浪潮”上台，政治风向已然彻底转变。 即将成为参议院多数党领袖的参议员Chuck Schumer在X平台上明确表态： “尽管黄仁勋已经辞职，国会必须要求他及英伟达其他人员交代他们可能如何将美国国家安全置于危险之中。” 他强调，美国人有权知道，身处权力最高层的人应当将国家利益放在首位，而不是个人的底线或友谊。 帝国式CEO的控制权反思与未来走向 尽管黄仁勋的下台凸显了权力的流失，但他在科技界的影响力可能并未彻底终结。马斯克周三表示，如果能聘请黄仁勋将是“一种荣幸”。前Twitter首席执行官Dick Costolo更是预测： “未来3到4年内，如果英伟达业绩出现一两个季度的下滑，他们将把黄仁勋请回来继续管理公司。美国人最喜欢的就是东山再起的故事。” 从公司治理的深层逻辑来看， 部分科技界人士认为此事件的最大教训并非黄仁勋的判断失误，而是他缺乏对公司的绝对公司治理控制权。 这种绝对控制权正是马斯克在SpaceX、马克·扎克伯格在Meta所拥有的，也是Anthropic创始人即将获得的。 不可否认，“帝国式CEO”的时代依然存在，但黄仁勋的黯然离场无疑是对硅谷权力极限的一次冷酷提醒。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 量化投资巨头文艺复兴科技（Renaissance Technologies）第三季度大幅调整股票组合，在英伟达丑闻发酵前，就早已几乎清仓该股，同时大举增持美光科技、AMD及闪迪。 根据最新提交的13F文件，截至9月30日， 文艺复兴科技持有的英伟达股票从第二季度末的709万股降至2.317万股，减持99.7%。Meta持股则从202万股降至1577股，减持99.9%，两家公司的持仓几乎被清空。 与大幅削减英伟达形成鲜明对比的是， 文艺复兴科技将美光持股增加618.7%至152万股，期末持仓市值约16.2亿美元。 AMD持股增加140.5%至近200万股，持仓价值约12.1亿美元，闪迪持股也大幅增加。 此外，文艺复兴科技新建SpaceX头寸，并调整医疗健康及金融板块配置。截至第三季度末，其披露的股票持仓总市值达到734.24亿美元，较第二季度末增长1.1%。不过，持仓市值变化并不等同于基金投资收益。 英伟达、Meta持仓几乎清零 文艺复兴科技第三季度大幅削减英伟达和Meta持仓，两家公司的股票几乎被清出其披露的投资组合。 截至9月30日，该公司持有英伟达2.317万股，较第二季度末的709万股减少99.7%，期末持仓价值约530万美元。Meta持股则从202万股降至1577股，减持99.9%，期末持仓价值约120万美元。 减持并不限于上述两家公司。第三季度，文艺复兴科技将亚马逊持股削减99.5%，苹果持股削减99.8%，台积电持股减少85.1%，博通持股减少99.9%。 Palantir也遭大幅减持，持股减少70.6%，减持规模估算约10亿美元。截至季度末，该公司仍持有约222万股Palantir股票，价值约4.16亿美元。 美光、AMD与闪迪获大幅增持 在削减多只大型科技股持仓的同时，文艺复兴科技显著增加对存储芯片及其他半导体公司的配置。 美光成为其第三季度重点增持标的之一。 该公司持股增加618.7%至152万股，期末持仓市值约16.2亿美元，占披露股票组合的2.2%。按照季度末股价估算，增持金额约14亿美元。 AMD持股增加140.5%至近200万股，期末持仓价值约12.1亿美元，增持金额估算约7.04亿美元。闪迪持股则从4980股增加至27.65万股，增幅达5451%，期末持仓市值约4.81亿美元。 从持仓变化来看，文艺复兴科技第三季度一方面大幅削减英伟达等大型科技股，另一方面显著提高对美光、AMD和闪迪的配置。但13F文件仅披露季度末持仓，无法直接揭示具体交易时点、价格及投资决策依据。 新建SpaceX头寸，增持医疗健康及金融股 除半导体板块外，文艺复兴科技第三季度还建立了新的SpaceX头寸，持有411.32万股，期末价值约6.205亿美元。 医疗健康领域同样获得增持。UnitedHealth Group持股增加506.7%，期末持仓价值约8.17亿美元。 金融板块方面，文艺复兴科技新建美国银行头寸，持仓价值约3.513亿美元，同时持有高盛约2.448亿美元。 持仓总市值升至734亿美元 截至第三季度末，文艺复兴科技披露的股票持仓总市值达到734.24亿美元，较第二季度末的726亿美元增长1.1%，涉及3151个持仓。 从行业分布来看，科技行业占其披露持仓价值的23.8%，医疗健康行业占15.7%，工业、可选消费和金融服务分别占10.6%、10.5%和10.3%。 基金业绩方面，据彭博报道，文艺复兴科技旗下Institutional Equities Fund在10月上涨6%，年内收益率达到12.3%。 需要注意的是，13F文件反映的是截至9月30日的持仓情况，并非实时投资组合。持仓市值变化也不等同于投资收益，其变化受到买卖操作及股价波动等因素影响。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 英伟达新掌门会给AI融资踩刹车？她曾将2500亿美元数据中心担保砍半，被黄仁勋嘲讽“只会做财务”，是“惊弓之鹿”
articles.summary: 黄仁勋的突然出局，不仅终结了英伟达一个时代，更动摇了整个AI生态系统赖以运转的融资基础。 过去三年，英伟达在黄仁勋主导下扮演着"AI中央银行"的角色，以股权投资、信贷担保和租约兜底织就一张规模逾5000亿美元的循环融资网络，为这个仍在烧钱的行业持续输血。如今，这位创始人因婚外情丑闻黯然离场，接棒者正是他曾当面羞辱为"惊弓之鹿"、斥之为"只会做财务"的首席财务官Colette Kress。 据《华尔街日报》报道， 此前正是Kress主动将英伟达对OpenAI俄亥俄州数据中心的兜底承诺从最初谈判的2500亿美元砍至约1050亿美元，也是她在融资担保项目快速扩张期间，一再追问如何为担保定价、如何计算投资回报。 在市场看来，这位新掌门让英伟达的资产负债表更安全，却让所有指望英伟达下一张支票的AI公司陷入了更深的不确定性。 高盛分析师James Schneider指出，现有承诺大概率会被履行，但"没有黄仁勋的视野、人脉和召集力，下一轮同等规模的多方生态投资将更难落地"。 一张超过5000亿美元的循环融资网 要理解黄仁勋离职的冲击，首先需要理解他搭建的这台融资机器有多大。 据英伟达7月26日的10-Q文件，公司的或有负债与承诺总规模已达5305亿美元。这一数字尚未涵盖7月后新签的交易，以及黄仁勋8月宣布的那个目标规模高达5000亿美元的AI计算融资平台中英伟达承诺提供的最多1250亿美元、即25%的兜底。 机制几乎一成不变： 英伟达买入股权或提供担保，受益方承诺采购英伟达硬件，资金以GPU订单的形式回流。 Safe Superintelligence尚未推出任何产品，便获得了Vera Rubin架构的大规模算力承诺；Meta追加了Vera Rubin、Spectrum-X和BlueField-4的订单；Nebius与IREN签署5GW部署协议—— 钱以股权形式流出，以营收形式回来。 俄亥俄州数据中心项目是这套逻辑最极端的呈现。据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达最终向OpenAI提供了1050亿美元的租约信贷担保，并可选择追加3.8GW算力。而据英伟达自身的CFO口径，俄亥俄园区每一代基础设施部署约等于150万块GPU，对应英伟达约1500亿至2000亿美元的营收—— 换言之，英伟达用1050亿美元的担保换取最高2000亿美元的芯片销售，周而复始，为期20年。 彭博社援引Panmure Liberum的警告称，"英伟达银行"是这家芯片公司的护城河，同时也是一个信用风险来源——有限的自由现金流被大规模承诺给一个仍在努力实现商业变现的行业。 黄仁勋亲手踩下刹车，Kress早已是幕后制动者 黄仁勋本人在辞职前已察觉这场扩张的隐患。 据《华尔街日报》报道，今年8月他将顶级财务高管召集到办公室，直言英伟达正陷入"一场麻烦"：公司正在与大量无力支付芯片费用的企业谈判提供担保，部分交易由其女婿、今年1月晋升为副总裁的Nico Caprez主导推进。Caprez与另一名副总裁Raj Mirpuri曾在春季向潜在合作伙伴承诺，英伟达可以在数周内完成信贷支持安排，条件是对方同意分享一定比例的营收，数十家公司随即排队等候。 在这次会议上，黄仁勋还当场打断了Kress的汇报，称她是"惊弓之鹿"，不过是一个"汇报型CFO"，而非能够参与战略决策的人。 与此同时，他描述了公司面临的真正危机： 大型云计算服务商正在加速转向替代芯片、削减对英伟达的依赖，而英伟达已承诺采购的大量晶圆和内存正"如雪崩般"扑来。 据英伟达财报，相关供应承诺在短短三个月内从约580亿美元激增至约2790亿美元。 就在黄仁勋发出"雪崩预警"之前，制动动作已由Kress悄然启动。 据《华尔街日报》报道，正是她将英伟达对OpenAI俄亥俄项目的担保规模从初步谈判的2500亿美元压缩至最终落地的1050亿美元，并持续在内部质疑担保项目的定价逻辑与回报测算。8月下旬，英伟达宣布暂停部分收入分成式信贷支持交易，要求所有新交易须经高管团队及董事会审查。10月，黄仁勋在柏林会见数家主要客户CEO时，以日本汤面师傅的故事为喻，向在场的云计算公司高管传递了一个明确信号："你们不是在决定我产品的价值。" 5000亿美元融资平台：高调亮相，零成交 今年8月，黄仁勋身着标志性皮夹克，在六大全球顶级资产管理机构高管的簇拥下宣布这一融资平台，试图将GPU打造成可供金融机构投资的资产类别——思路类似房地产或收费公路的证券化，将快速折旧的硬件转化为可担保的基础设施资产。 然而，据彭博社报道，该平台迄今未能落地任何一笔交易，六家机构与英伟达签署的仍是初步意向备忘录，尚未形成最终协议。 障碍之一是兜底比例。 英伟达目前提供的剩余价值支持上限为交易规模的25%，而竞争对手博通已为今年5月Anthropic一笔350亿美元债务交易提供了约86%的兜底，并将为另一笔630亿美元交易提供约72.5%的担保。面对如此悬殊的差距，部分客户和华尔街合作伙伴已向英伟达施压，要求提高兜底比例。据彭博社报道，该平台最早或要到明年1月才可能宣布首笔交易——前提是黄仁勋的离职不影响相关进程。 Raymond James全球私募资本咨询业务负责人Sunaina Sinha Haldea对CNBC表示，管理层更迭为所有参与方提供了一个天然的"暂停键"，重新审视交易条款。她不认为资本会就此撤离，但警告称，"他们可能要求为这种不确定性索取更高回报"。她还预计，贷款方的追问将蔓延至整个AI基础设施交易市场：谁在真正承担这些结构中的风险？ Kress接棒：收紧的手，复杂的局面 从黄仁勋鄙视的"汇报型CFO"，到英伟达史上首位女性临时CEO，Kress的上位充满戏剧性。熟悉英伟达投资决策的人士表示，Kress此前曾多次对黄仁勋力推的交易提出异议， 预计不会以接近黄仁勋的速度推进新交易。 高盛分析师James Schneider在下调英伟达目标价后指出， 英伟达将履行所有已宣布的承诺，但下一轮大规模多方生态投资将因缺乏黄仁勋的个人资源与号召力而更难推进。 高盛还特别指出，英伟达股票此前已在折价交易，部分原因正是市场担忧： 一旦英伟达或其竞争对手停止提供融资，AI基础设施增长将急剧放缓。 瑞银分析师Tim Arcuri在报告中将"融资"列为黄仁勋离职的三大核心影响之首，并估算英伟达每季度500亿至600亿美元的自由现金流中有很大一部分被回流至客户、供应商和新兴云计算商，即便只是短暂暂停，也可能从AI生态系统中抽走500亿美元以上——时机恰逢利率上行、信贷市场流动性收紧。 William Blair分析师Sebastien Naji则认为，现有合同将在CEO更迭后存续，但受威胁的是下一轮交易，以及英伟达在2027年及以后捍卫市场份额的能力。随着黄仁勋离去或受制于调查，博通和AMD等竞争对手或将获得更大的市场空间。 已定与未定：哪些交易将受冲击 外界目前认为，已签署具有法律约束力合同的投资预计不受影响。英伟达拟投资50亿美元的Safe Superintelligence，以及拟向Mira Murati创立的Thinking Machines Lab投资约25亿美元的交易，合同均已于数月前签署，预计将如期落地。 受冲击更大的是仍处于谈判阶段的交易。 英伟达拟在Anthropic即将进行的IPO中投资100亿美元，能否延续尚不明朗；此前英伟达已向Anthropic提供了1050亿美元的数据中心租赁信贷担保。正在谈判为Nscale提供逾50亿美元信贷担保的协议，截至10月底尚未签署。澳大利亚云计算商Firmus在撤回IPO后寻求至少20亿美元私募融资，英伟达此前已参与谈判，结果未定。人形机器人公司Figure AI据报道正与英伟达讨论追加10亿美元投资，最新进展不详。 Saxo首席投资策略师Charu Chanana指出， 真正的风险不是个别合作关系的瓦解，而是在债务高企、循环融资和回报不确定性已被广泛质疑的当下，黄仁勋的离职可能触发AI生态系统整体风险溢价的重新定价——"这还不是一场融资危机，但可能成为更广泛风险重定价的催化剂。" Kress将在11月17日主持英伟达三季度财报电话会议，届时分析师必然追问她如何看待那5000亿美元的承诺，以及英伟达是否将继续扮演"AI央行"的角色。这将是黄仁勋离职后，市场对那台循环融资机器能否延续运转、最直接的一次测试。 风险提示及免责条款
